description: Sync recorded Gong calls with their transcripts, AI content and public comments, plus coaching reviews and library placements, from the workspaces you choose. Gong permissions are not imported.
opening: Sync recorded calls from the Gong workspaces you select. Each call is one document holding the call details, linked CRM records, topics, Gong's AI brief, key points, highlights and outline, the full speaker-labelled transcript, and public comments. Each completed coaching review, and each call filed in a library folder, is its own document linked to the call.

Gong permissions are not imported, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Calls Gong marks private are skipped unless you turn them on. Changes that arrive after a call's re-read window, such as late comments, are missed. Audio and video are not synced.

notes: Calls Gong marks private, reviews of those calls, and reviews that are not public are skipped unless you turn on `include_private_calls`. With it on, they are synced without their Gong audience. Set an access rule on the workspace if they must stay restricted.
A call that Gong does not mark as private or public is synced. A review with no visibility is treated as public.
If HydraDB cannot read the privacy of the call behind a review or library placement, the item still syncs, with a permission warning.

connect.auth: Gong uses an API key pair, an Access Key and an Access Key Secret, created by a Gong technical administrator.

credentials.name: access_key_secret
credentials.text: The Gong Access Key Secret. Gong shows it once.

credentials.name: api_base_url
credentials.text: The HTTPS API host shown on Gong's API keys page: `api.gong.io`, or your company's subdomain directly before `api.gong.io`. Set it only if Gong shows a company-specific address.

credentials.name: include_private_calls
credentials.text: Off by default. Turn it on to also sync private calls and reviews that are not public.

credentials.name: transcript_settle_hours
credentials.text: How many hours of recent calls every sync reads again, to catch late transcripts, briefs and comments. 24 by default.

connect.permissions_label: Gong API permissions the connector uses

permissions.name: api:library:read
permissions.text: optional. Without it, library placements are skipped.

permissions.name: api:settings:scorecards:read
permissions.text: optional. Without it, coaching reviews are skipped.

permissions.name: api:stats:scorecards
permissions.text: optional. Without it, coaching reviews are skipped.

connect.permissions_note: A Gong API key pair covers the whole company and has no scope picker. The list names what the connector reads, not grants you choose. Which optional endpoints your Gong plan allows depends on your subscription.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.text: In Gong's Admin center, open Settings, Ecosystem, API, API keys, and choose Get API key. Only technical administrators can do this. Copy the Access Key and the Access Key Secret.

steps.title: Leave the expiry and IP limits empty
steps.text: Leave the key's TTL empty. A key with an expiry stops the connector on that date. Leave Trusted IPs empty unless you add HydraDB's outgoing addresses, or every request fails.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the Access Key as `access_key` and the secret as `access_key_secret`. If the API keys page shows a company-specific API address, enter it as `api_base_url`.

steps.title: Select workspaces
steps.text: HydraDB lists the company's Gong workspaces. Select the ones to sync. Each workspace syncs separately.

connect.account: One connector reads one Gong company, through its company-wide API key.

sync.first_sync: Calls and reviews reach back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. For calls, the window reaches back a further `transcript_settle_hours`. Library folders are read in full.
sync.changes: Each sync reads calls by start time, and reads again every call that started within the last `transcript_settle_hours`, 24 by default, to catch late transcripts, briefs and comments. Reviews are read by review time. The workspace library is read in full on every sync.
sync.edits: A call is updated only while its start time is inside the re-read window. Later changes to a call, such as a comment added after that, are missed. Raise `transcript_settle_hours` to keep calls open longer.
sync.deletes: Calls that disappear from Gong can stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: The shortest sync interval for Gong is 30 minutes.
Gong allows a company 10,000 API calls a day. HydraDB shares that allowance with every other integration on your Gong company.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Calls
documents.one_document: One recorded call, with its transcript and public comments.
documents.title: The call title, else `Gong call` and the call id.
documents.text: The title, then `When`, `Duration`, `Direction`, `Scope`, `Host`, `Participants` with their job titles, `Related` CRM records, `Outcome`, `Topics` and `Trackers` lines. Then `Brief`, `Key points`, `Highlights` and `Outline` sections, then `Transcript` with one line per speaker turn. Public comments are searchable with the call.
documents.files: None. Audio and video are never downloaded.

attributes.name: Transcript
attributes.text: The full transcript, one line per speaker turn, when Gong has produced it.

attributes.name: host
attributes.text: The host's name, written as the `Host` line. The graph records that person as the call's host.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.host_email
attributes.text: The host's email. Identifies the host across tools, and limits a query to one host. Written as the `Host` line only when the host's name is missing.

attributes.name: participants
attributes.text: Each party's name, email, job title and affiliation, written as the `Participants` line. The graph records each as a participant.

attributes.name: Public comments
attributes.text: The text of each public comment, searchable with the call. The graph records each comment's author.

attributes.name: brief
attributes.text: Gong's AI brief, in the `Brief` section.

attributes.name: key_points
attributes.text: Gong's AI key points, in the `Key points` section.

attributes.name: highlights
attributes.text: Gong's AI highlight headings and items, in the `Highlights` section.

attributes.name: action_items
attributes.text: The next steps from Gong's highlights, written as the call's action items.

attributes.name: outline
attributes.text: Gong's AI outline sections and items, in the `Outline` section, without timings.

attributes.name: topics
attributes.text: The topics discussed, written as the `Topics` line and as the call's labels. Topics with no talk time are left out.

attributes.name: trackers
attributes.text: The trackers that fired, with their counts, written as the `Trackers` line. Trackers that did not fire are left out.

attributes.name: crm_context
attributes.text: Linked CRM records as `ObjectType: Name`, written as the `Related` line, so a deal or account name finds the call. It does not link the call to a CRM record in the graph.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.text: The call length, written as the `Duration` line.

attributes.name: started_at
attributes.text: When the call actually started, written into the text.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.direction
attributes.text: Inbound, Outbound, Conference or Unknown, written as the `Direction` line. Separates inbound from outbound calls.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.scope
attributes.text: Internal, External or Unknown, written as the `Scope` line. Limits a query to customer-facing calls.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.call_outcome
attributes.text: The call outcome, such as Demo booked, written as the `Outcome` line. Limits a query to one outcome.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.crm_object_ids
attributes.text: Linked CRM records as `ObjectType:id` pairs. Finds every call linked to one CRM opportunity or account. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.primary_user_id
attributes.text: The host's Gong user id. Limits a query to one rep's calls. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.media
attributes.text: Video or Audio. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.language
attributes.text: The detected language. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_private
attributes.text: Gong's private flag. Leaves private calls out of a query when you sync them. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.has_transcript
attributes.text: Whether the transcript has arrived. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.calendar_event_id
attributes.text: The calendar event id. Finds the call for a known calendar event. It is not linked to calendar documents. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The workspace id. Limits a query to one workspace. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The workspace name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `workspace`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: scheduled_at
attributes.text: When the call was scheduled to start. It is not the result date.

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.text: The call's purpose label.

attributes.name: system
attributes.text: The conferencing or telephony system that recorded the call.

attributes.name: comment_count
attributes.text: How many non-empty public comments the call has.

documents.name: Coaching reviews
documents.one_document: One completed scorecard review of one call.
documents.title: The scorecard name, `review of`, the rep reviewed, and the call date.
documents.text: The title, then `Reviewer`, `Reviewed`, `Reviewed at`, `Method` and `Call id` lines, then each question with its score, selected options and answer text. A question that does not apply shows `N/A`. `Author` and `Updated` lines are part of the text too.
documents.date: When the review was completed, else when the call started.

attributes.name: answers
attributes.text: Each question with its score, selected options and answer text. The structured answers are kept with the review too.

attributes.name: scorecard_name
attributes.text: The scorecard's name, in the title.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.text: The reviewer, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the review as written by that person.

attributes.name: reviewer
attributes.text: The reviewer, or Gong AI, written as the `Reviewer` line.

attributes.name: reviewed_user
attributes.text: The rep reviewed, in the title and the `Reviewed` line. The rep is not attached to the review as a person.

attributes.name: review_time
attributes.text: When the review was completed, written as the `Reviewed at` and `Updated` lines. Also kept as the review's created and updated time.

attributes.name: call_started_at
attributes.text: When the reviewed call started, in the title. Used as the result date only when the review time is missing.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The reviewer's email. Identifies the reviewer in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The call the review scores. Links the review to that call. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.call_id
attributes.text: The reviewed call. Returns every review of one call. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.scorecard_id
attributes.text: The scorecard. Limits a query to one scorecard. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.review_method
attributes.text: `MANUAL` or `AUTOMATIC`. Separates human and AI reviews. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.reviewer_user_id
attributes.text: The reviewer's Gong user id. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.reviewer_email
attributes.text: The reviewer's email. Limits a query to one reviewer. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.reviewed_user_id
attributes.text: The reviewed rep's Gong user id. Finds every review of one rep. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.reviewed_email
attributes.text: The reviewed rep's email. Finds every review of one rep. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.visibility_type
attributes.text: The review's Gong visibility. Leaves out reviews that are not public, when you sync them. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The scorecard's workspace id. Limits a query to one workspace. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The workspace name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `workspace`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: answer_count
attributes.text: How many answers the review contains.

documents.name: Library placements
documents.one_document: One call filed in one library folder. A call filed in two folders is two documents.
documents.title: The call title, then `(filed in` and the folder path.
documents.text: The title, then the folder, who filed the call and when, and the curator's note. `Space`, `Author` and `Updated` lines are part of the text too.
documents.link_back: The placement in Gong, when Gong supplies its address.

attributes.name: note
attributes.text: The curator's note, under `Curator note`.

attributes.name: folder_path
attributes.text: The folder and up to eight parent folders, in the title and the `Library folder` line.

attributes.name: space_name
attributes.text: The folder path, written as the `Space` line, so a folder name finds the call.

attributes.name: call_title
attributes.text: The original call title, in the title and the text.

attributes.name: filed_by
attributes.text: Who filed the call, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the placement as written by that person.

attributes.name: filed_at
attributes.text: When the call was filed, written as the `Filed at` and `Updated` lines. Also kept as the placement's created and updated time.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The filer's email. Identifies the filer in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The filed call. Links the placement to that call. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.call_id
attributes.text: The filed call. Returns every placement of one call. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.folder_id
attributes.text: The library folder. Limits a query to one folder. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.filed_by_user_id
attributes.text: The filer's Gong user id. Limits a query to one curator. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.library_container_type
attributes.text: Always `library_folder`. Separates placements from calls. Not searchable.

attributes.name: space_id
attributes.text: The library folder id. Filter on it with `additional_metadata.folder_id`.

attributes.name: snippet_from_sec
attributes.text: Where the filed excerpt starts in the call, in seconds, when only part of the call was filed.

attributes.name: snippet_to_sec
attributes.text: Where the filed excerpt ends in the call, in seconds.

example_searches: What objections did Acme raise on our last three calls?
How did Jordan score on the discovery scorecard last month?
Which calls are in the Best discovery calls library folder, and why were they filed?

connections: A coaching review to the call it scores.
A library placement to the call it files.
CRM record ids and calendar event ids are kept for filtering only. They do not link a call to CRM or calendar documents.
people: The host and every participant of each call, with their email when Gong has it.
The author of each public comment.
The reviewer of each coaching review, and the person who filed each library placement.
The rep reviewed is not attached to the review as a person.
graph.from_text: The transcript and Gong's AI content for each call, coaching review answers and curator notes.

not_synced: Emails and other digital interactions, Engage flows and tasks, and forecasts.
Audio and video, per-person interaction statistics, and transcript timings.
Private calls, reviews of them, and reviews that are not public, unless `include_private_calls` is on.
Private and archived library folders, even with `include_private_calls` on.
Library placements or coaching reviews when Gong refuses the optional endpoint. Reviews also need access to scorecard definitions.
Comments and other changes that arrive after a call's re-read window.
